definitions.definition: For r>0 such that e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E(r) is the finite real Lebesgue integral ∫ e(x,r) dx. This definition assigns no value at times for which integrability has not been established.

definitions.definition: For each positive integer k, identify ℝᵏ with the finite product Fin k→ℝ, equip it with its Euclidean norm and topology, the Borel σ-algebra generated by that topology, and product Lebesgue measure (the product of one-dimensional Lebesgue volume on each coordinate).

The ambient measurable space on ℝⁿ is the Borel σ-algebra generated by its Euclidean topology, and Lebesgue measure μ satisfies μ(K)<∞ for every compact K⊂ℝⁿ.
For each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), compact C_J exists with u=q outside C_J throughout J.
For topological spaces X,Y and compact subsets s⊆X,t⊆Y, the product s×t is compact.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r>0. Choose J=[r/2,3r/2], a compact interval contained in (0,∞) with r in its interior, and choose compact C from H003 for this J. Define C*=C∪{0}; it is compact and nonempty. The support condition implies u=q off C* for every τ∈J, hence all time and spatial derivatives occurring in e_t vanish there. The function (x,τ)↦|e_t(x,τ)| is continuous on C*×J by smoothness, and C*×J is compact by M005; apply M019 with target ℝ to obtain a finite real bound K≥0 with |e_t(x,τ)|≤K on C*×J. Define b(x)=K·1_{C*}(x). Then |e_t(x,τ)|≤b(x) for all x and τ∈J, including x outside C* where e_t=0. By N001, C* is measurable and has finite measure. Apply M008 to the constant K on C* and M009 to its indicator extension to obtain integrability of b on all ℝⁿ. Define F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and Fprime(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ). For each τ∈J these are continuous in x by N001; under the Euclidean topology/Borel measurable structure on ℝⁿ, ℝ is pseudo-metrizable, and Euclidean ℝⁿ is second-countable, so M020 applies to each continuous section and gives a.e. strong measurability of F(τ) and Fprime(τ). In particular F(r) is integrable by N001 and Fprime(r) is a.e. strongly measurable. For each x, smoothness gives HasDerivAt (τ↦F(τ)(x)) (Fprime(τ)(x)) τ throughout the open interval (r/2,3r/2). M006 applies with α=ℝⁿ, μ=Lebesgue measure, scalar and target ℝ, x₀=r, s=(r/2,3r/2), F, Fprime and bound b: the neighborhood condition holds; the near-r a.e. strong measurability follows from M020 at every τ in that neighborhood; base integrability is N001; derivative-section measurability is M020; the pointwise-a.e. derivative condition holds everywhere by smoothness; domination holds everywhere by the bound above; and b is integrable. Its conclusion gives integrability of Fprime(r) and HasDerivAt of τ↦∫e(x,τ)dx with derivative ∫e_t(x,r)dx. By the guarded definition D002 (whose prerequisite N001 directly supplies integrability at r), this is differentiability of E at r and E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Arbitrary r proves the complete output.
